newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: 20TH CENTURY FOX INTERESTED IN S.AFRICAN FILMS.
newsitem.headline: 20TH CENTURY FOX INTERESTED IN S.AFRICAN FILMS.

text.p: Hollywood's 20th Century Fox is interested in buying films from post-apartheid South Africa, the company said on Friday.

"We're actively looking for product," Michael Jenkinson, vice-president of acquisitions and production at the company, told a seminar at the Southern African International Film and Television Market in Cape Town.
"I suppose I came here for a lot of different reasons, one is curiosity. I've always been fascinated by South Africa," he said.
"From a business standpoint I think it's another developing market and we have a responsibility...to stimulate the growth in regional markets and to help these markets develop."
Jenkinson said South Africa, which has a turbulent history of race war, had tremendous potential as a source of films.
"I think there's a great opportunity here -- there's interesting cultures, a rich history, a lot of diversity, it's English language for the most part...it's another potential source of product.

"There's a lot of curiosity about this marketplace and to see what direction it's going to take. Obviously there's an infrastructure and a film-making history and tradition," Jenkinson said, adding that South Africa could become another Australia in terms of film-making.
"Somebody who grows up outside North American culture brings a new perspective, different ideas...It's something we've all come to appreciate," he said.
